views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not fire new tariffs or non-tariff measures before the United States actually imposes List 3. Reopen talks immediately at a higher political level than the August 22–23 Malpass–Wang meetings, keep the already-announced $60 billion contingent list as the automatic reply if List 3 goes live, and treat extra US purchases as a bargaining chip rather than a pre-concession. Hold the yuan in an orderly range and do not reopen the ZTE wound with new firm-level measures against US companies in China.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. The United States has already put 25% tariffs on the full $50 billion Section 301 package (List 1 on 6 July, List 2 on 23 August) aimed at Made in China 2025 sectors, and USTR’s proposed List 3 (~$200 billion, rate under review from 10% to 25%) sits at the end of its comment window on 5–6 September and could be imposed immediately after. That is a material hit to the export machine and to industrial-policy goals, and the April ZTE denial order showed Washington can freeze a national champion by cutting US components. FX pressure is already visible: CNY weakened from about 6.33 to 6.83 per dollar (~8%) between mid-March and 5 September, industrial production slowed from 107.0 to 105.8, and reserves slipped about $37 billion. It is not +0.5/existential because merchandise exports are still rising (front-loading), the ZTE ban was lifted on 13 July after a $1.4 billion settlement, and reserves remain ~$3.1 trillion. Action should stay near hold/negotiate rather than escalate: China already matched the $50 billion dollar-for-dollar and on 3 August announced a $60 billion 5–25% list because it is running out of US goods (2017 US exports to China were only ~$154 billion). Trump’s 18 June statement already ties a further $200 billion to any new Chinese retaliation, so firing first would expand the war onto terrain we cannot match. The May 19 purchase-truce collapsed ten days later when the White House proceeded with 301, so conceding purchases or structural MIC 2025 reforms now would be unilateral and unreciprocated. August 22–23 talks were candid but empty; keep the channel open to delay or narrow List 3, and only implement the $60 billion list if Washington actually moves.
key_factors: Imminent US List 3 (~$200B, possibly 25%) as comment period ends 5–6 Sept
China already matched the $50B package and has only ~$60B of usable US imports left
CNY down ~8% with PBOC reintroducing the counter-cyclical factor to stop a run toward 7
ZTE denial order demonstrated a US component kill-switch, then was settled rather than left in place
May 19 purchase truce collapsed on 29 May; August talks produced no new US offer
Chinese exports and IP still holding; threat is rising but not yet a financial-stability event

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines).
At Trump's direction, USTR says it is considering raising the proposed List 3 rate from 10% to 25%.
List 2 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$16B (completing the $50B package). China imposes matching ~$16B retaliation.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against the $50B action.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China industrial production index eased from 107.0 (Apr) to 105.8 (Sep).
China reserves ex-gold fell from $3,144bn (Apr) to $3,106bn (Sep), about -$37bn.
China merchandise exports still rose from $208.6bn (Apr) to $216.3bn (Sep); real-economy hit not yet decisive.
China announced a $60B retaliation list (5–25% on 5,207 lines) if the US proceeds with List 3; remaining US goods are limited by the lopsided trade balance.
Aug 22–23 talks produced no compromises; MOFCOM called them constructive and said both sides would keep in contact. List 3 comment period ends Sept 6.
US lifted the ZTE ban on 13 July after a $1bn penalty, $400mn escrow, board overhaul, and 10-year monitors.
PBOC reintroduced the counter-cyclical factor on Aug 24 after the yuan’s 10-week slide toward 6.93; officials vowed not to use depreciation as a weapon.
